newsitem.title: UK: Deutsche exit reduces London metal ring to 15.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche exit reduces London metal ring to 15.

text.p: Investment bank Deutsche Morgan Grenfell (DMG) said on Wednesday that it is to relinquish its London Metal Exchange (LME) membership and that some staff would be leaving the firm.

"As part of the continuing integration and enhancement of the commodity operations within Deutsche Morgan Grenfell we have decided to re-focus our LME operations and relinquish our ring membership," the London-based firm said.
A news release said it remained firmly committed to the base metals business and that its interests would be served by being an LME Associate Broker Clearing Member.

A spokesman for DMG which is the investment banking arm of Germany's Deutsche Bank said the company would be adopting its new status with immediate effect and would not man the trading floor on Wednesday afternoon. Some staff would be leaving the company.
The firm employed about five people on the floor.
The decision reduces the number of LME ring dealing members to 15.

Last November 21 another firm, Lehman Brothers Commodities, quit the floor of the LME in what was seen at the time as the latest and largest in a series of adjustments on the metals market since the Sumitomo scandal erupted a year ago this weekend.

Activity on the LME, hub of the global trade in metals, had slumped since mid-June 1996 when Sumitomo Corp of Japan fired star trader Yasuo Hamanaka, alleging he ran up losses of $2.6 billion in unauthorised copper trading.
But volumes, except in copper, picked up early in 1997.

DMG were described as middle players on the LME by other brokers. "To some extent liquidity may dry up," said Robin Bhar, analyst at brokerage Brandeis, asked to assess the impact of the DMG decision.
"But others will pick up more business. The LME wasn't their core activity".
